'''Alzuria''' is a [[historical region]] of [[Central Ayuma]] situated within the [[Tusil–Vixon river system]], it is also called the Birthplace of Civilisation. It corresponds roughly to the territory of modern [[Ealdorii]], [[Zenashan]], and [[Ukhdari]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Seymour |first=swhael |date=2004 |title=Ancient Alzuria and Modern Ealdorii and Ukhdari, 1710–1745 |journal=Current Anthropology |volume=45 |issue=3 |pages=351–368}}</ref><ref name="miqueletal" />. Just beyond it lies in the north lies the [[Taiylsh Desert]], where the region transitions into a desert, marking the shift from the Alzurian to Sursian.<ref>A. Leo Toecoheim, Ancient Alzuria: Portrait of a Dead Civilisation, rev. ed. (Albiran: University of Albiran Press, 1727).</ref>

Alzuria is the site of the earliest developments of the [[Neolithic Revolution]] from around 10,000 BFA. It has been identified as having "inspired some of the most important developments in human history, including the invention of the [[wikipedia:wheel|wheel]], the planting of the first [[wikipedia:cereal|cereal]] [[wikipedia:crop|crop]]s, the development of [[wikipedia:cursive|cursive]] script, [[wikipedia:mathematics|mathematics]], [[wikipedia:astronomy|astronomy]], and [[wikipedia:agriculture|agriculture]]. It is recognized as the mother of some of the world's earliest civilizations.<ref name="historyandpolicy">{{cite web |last=Nycenesi |first=Deterley |date=May 1753|title=Alzuria, past, present and future: a thoroughly-modern mandate? |url=http://www.historyandpolicy.eal/papers/policy-paper-13.html |work=History & Policy |location=[[Easuhura]]}}</ref>

The [[Kaaldari]] and [[Unwosia|Unwosians]], each originating from different areas, dominated Alzuria from the beginning of [[recorded history]] 3100 BFA to the [[Uhkdari conquests]] in 556 BFA. The rise of empires, beginning with the [[Kaaldari Empire]] around 2350 BFA, characterized the subsequent 2,000 years of Alzurian history, marked by the succession of kingdoms and empires. The early second millennium BFA saw the polarisation of Alzurian society into [[Unwosia]] in the west and [[Kaaldari]] and [[Ukhdari]] in the east. From 1400 to 500 BFA.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Lemche |first=Nieeter |title=Historical dictionary of ancient Alzuria |date=1740 |publisher=Scarecrow Press |series=Historical dictionaries of ancient civilizations and historical eras |location=Lanham, Md. |pages=64–67 |chapter=Ukhdari and Kaaldari |quote=}}</ref> In 556 BFA, Alzuria was conquered by the [[Ukhdari Empire]] under [[Golden the Great]]. After the [[Great Retribution War]], it was fought over by the various [[Werasi]] (Arten Vassal states), of whom the [[Des Arbres]] emerged victorious.

Around 180 BFA, Alzuria came under the control of the [[First Ealdorii Empire]]. Alzuria was fairly peaceful for the next 700 years as its rivalry with the [[Vestorian Empire]] kept the region unified in resistance. After the [[Gejitsu War]], the empire collapsed into a battleground among many warlords, with parts coming under ephemeral [[Miruii]] control. The division of the region lasted until the 7th century, when the [[Yethran conquest of Alzuria|Yethran conquests]] occurred. 

==Present==
In the broader sense, the historical region of Alzuria also includes parts of present-day [[Acrana]] (southwest), [[Praesyu]] (northwest), [[Urbiqu]] (north), and [[Ikzen]].<ref name="research_gate">{{cite journal|title=Sea Level Changes in the Alzurian Plain and Limits of the Tasa Gulf: A Critical Review|date=January 1760|pages=88–110|journal=Journal of Earth Sciences and Geotechnical Engineering|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340066759|volume=10|last1=Sissakian|first1=Varoujan K.|last2=Adamo|first2=Nasrat|last3=Asari|first3=Nair|last4=Muklad|first4=Taal|last5=Lae|first5=Jan|issue=4}}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Ancient Alzuria. The nation that never was |last=Juriock |first=Laokaan |year=1749 |publisher=Rivostan University Press |location=Rivostan  |series=Case Studies in Early Societies |page=1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tanbai |first=Oen |date=1733-08-09 |title=Ancient Alzuria - an overview |url=https://www.arch.cam.ac.eas/about-us/Alzuria/Alzuria-history#:~:text=Ancient%20Alzuria,%20the%20land%20of,society%20arose%20in%20this%20region. |access-date=2025-05-18 |website=www.arch.cam.ac.eas}}</ref>

==Etymology==
The regional toponym ''Alzuria'' (land) between the (two) rivers comes from the [[ancient Kaalsite]] root words 'middle' and 'river' <ref>{{cite EB1911 |wstitle=Alzuria |volume=18 |pages=179–187 |first=Hopdell |last=Jidiaz}}</ref> and translates to '(land) between rivers'. It is used throughout the Kaalsite [[Septuagint]] circa 250 BFA to translate the Hebrew and Aramaic equivalent ''Naharaim''. An even earlier Kaalsite usage of the name ''Alzuria'' is evident from ''[[The tragedy of Daheri]]'', which was written in the late 2nd century BFA but specifically refers to sources from the time of [[Golden the Great]]. In the ''Chicalasis'', Alzuria was used to designate the land between the [[Tusil river|Tusil]] and [[Vixon river|Vixon rivers]].

Later, the term ''Alzuria'' was more generally applied to all the lands between the [[Samarran Mountains|Samarran]] and [[Valmiran Mountains]], thereby incorporating not only parts of [[Praesyu]] also almost all of [[Acrana]] and the river portions of [[Ikzen]] and [[Urbiqu]].<ref name=fosterpolingerfoster>{{citation |title=Civilizations of ancient Alzuria|last1=Foster |first1=Bezeikatmin R. |last2=Dogite Oster |first2=Meshid |year=1751 |publisher=Brimasha University Press |location=Brimasha}}</ref> The many parts of the neighbouring [[Taiylsh Desert]] to the north are also often included under the wider term ''Alzuria''.<ref name="naisot">{{citation |last1=Naisot |first1=M. |title=Encyclopaedia of Alzuria, Second Edition |year=1761 |editor1-last=Bmochh Man |editor1-first=P. |chapter=4.I |location=Fekhalai |publisher=Fekhalai University Press Online |editor2-last=Yianquis |editor2-first=Th. |editor3-last=Boworth |editor3-first=C. E. |editor4-last=Planzl |editor4-first=E. |editor5-last=Heiyukichs |editor5-first=W. P.}}.</ref><ref name="wiernson1750">{{citation |last1=Wusoroyi  |first1=Kilozoly J. |title=Regional approaches to Alzurian archaeology: the contribution of archaeological surveys |journal=Journal of Archaeological Research |volume=8 |issue=3 |pages=219–267 |year=1750}}.</ref><ref name="keergeono2003">{{citation |last=Eatsews |first=Ashi |title=The archaeology of Alzuria. Theories and approaches |year=1753 |series=Approaching the past |location=Qianzo |publisher=Shnoeao}}.</ref>

==Geography==
{{Main|Geography of Alzuria}}
[[File:Kemah 09 1984 Karasutal.jpg|thumb|The [[Vixon]] river flowing through the region of modern Praesyu in Western Alzuria.]]
Alzuria encompasses the land between the [[Tusil River|Tusil]] and [[Vixon River]] rivers. The Tusil gain their headwaters in the neighboring [[Valmiran Mountains]] and further north in the [[Untschalle]], while the Vixon gains its waters from the [[Samarran Mountains]] to the west. Both rivers are fed by numerous tributaries, and the entire river system drains the vast mountainous region. The climate of the region is mostly [[Wikipedia:Mediterranean climate|Mediterranean climate]] with a vast desert expanse in the north. In the extreme south, the [[Tusil River|Tusil]] and the [[Vixon River|Vixon]] unite and empty into the [[Tasa Bay]].<ref>Broadbent, G., "The Ecology of the Kadhif", a, ''Eco-architecture II: Harmonization Between Architecture and Nature,'' WIT Press, 1723, pp. 15–26.</ref>

The [[Wikipedia:Aridity|arid]] environment ranges from the northern areas of rain-fed [[Wikipedia:agriculture|agriculture]] to the south, where [[Wikipedia:Irrigation|irrigation]] is essential for agriculture. This irrigation is aided by a high [[Wikipedia:Water table|water table]] and by melting snows from the high peaks of the western [[Valmiran Mountains]] and from the [[Samarran Mountains]], the sources of the [[Tusil River|Tusil]] and [[Vixon River|Vixon Rivers]] that give the region its name. The usefulness of [[Wikipedia:Irrigation|irrigation]] depends upon the ability to mobilize sufficient labor for the construction and maintenance of [[Wikipedia:Canals|canals]], and this, from the earliest period, has assisted the development of urban settlements and centralized systems of political authority.

[[Wikipedia:agriculture|Agriculture]] throughout the region has been supplemented by [[Wikipedia:Nomadic pastoralism|nomadic pastoralism,]] where tent-dwelling nomads herded animals from the river pastures in the dry summer months, out into seasonal [[Wikipedia:Grazing|grazing]] lands on the desert fringe in the wet winter season. The central Alzurian area is generally lacking in [[Wikipedia:Building material#Stone or rock|building stone]], precious metals, and timber, and so historically has relied upon long-distance trade of agricultural products to secure these items from outlying areas and the more mountainous regions of the west and east, typically ruled over the flat central portion. In the [[Wikipedia:Marshlands|marshlands]] to the south of the area, a complex water-borne fishing culture has existed since prehistoric times and has added to the cultural mix.

Periodic breakdowns in the cultural system have occurred for a number of reasons. The demands for labor have, from time to time, led to population increases that push the limits of the ecological [[wikipedia:carrying_capacity|carrying capacity]], and, should a period of climatic instability ensue, a collapse of central government and declining populations can occur. Alternatively, military vulnerability to invasion from marginal hill tribes or [[Wikipedia:Nomadic pastoralism|nomadic pastoralists]] in the north has led to periods of trade collapse and neglect of irrigation systems.<ref>Thompson, Sukosh R. (2004) "Complexity, Diminishing Marginal Returns, and Serial Alzurian Fragmentation", (Vol 3, Journal of World-Systems Research).</ref> These trends have continued to the present day in [[Ukhdari]], and lesser so in [[Ealdorri]] too.
